title: migrating game from 2D to 3D after discovering Blender MCP
author: Fizassist1
selftext:
Well this has been quite the process!  I was having many issues with 2D, especially with perspective and the character creator.  I decided to make the 3d character creator first to see if moving to 3D would solve my issues, and quickly found out it was worth the time and effort.



I used Claude+blenderMCP+godot for the initial 3D character creator.  Once I was happy with that, I moved on to 3D modeling the lab with the same process.  I managed to stay very faithful to my 2D versions dimensions, so it plays roughly the same (and previous players' data should be saved and familiar).  When my Claude 5hr was used up, I was experimenting with the main menu (using my 2d menu as reference) with Codex+blenderMCP+Godot instead of Claude.  I managed to get that to a version I liked, including adding a fly-in for both loading and into the lab.



When I upgraded the lab to 3D, I immediately saw the advantages and realized I would no longer have perspective issues.  I had to remodel every decoration unlock I had in 3D using the 2D sprites as reference.  I've iterated on them a bit, but there is still room for improvement in those models.  



The walk animation was funny at first.  My GF kept calling it the "67" walk because of how the model moved its arms.  However, enough was enough and I had astra give it go and it was an immediate improvement.  Outside of that, plus modeling the magic hammers, everything was done with Opus 5.  



Overall, it took about 2 weeks, since I just have the $20 plans.  But, it was absolutely worth it.  This is the latest capture I grabbed with all the features displayed in their 3D counterparts.  For example, the lab station notebooks didn't exist before.  It used to be just a popup UI.  Same with the lighting panel.



Okay I feel like I'm rambling now.  Let me know what you think!

For reference, the old 2D version is still the live one at the link below.  I still have some work to do before publishing my 3D update.

[learninglabphysics.com](http://learninglabphysics.com)

comments.author: Tommyruin
comments.body: The jump to 3d is a huge milestone. I'd definitely focus on polishing some things before you go further, as there's too many different styles going on here. Pixel art text and characters, cartoon characters, lots of conflicting fonts.
